review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the `conjOn` definitions elsewhere in the repo. I also read Mathlib's `Subgroup.centerCongr` and `map_center_eq` in Mathlib/GroupTheory/Subgroup/Center.lean. Most other repetition is routine: `cyc1_mem`/`cyc2_mem`, `ha3`/`hb3` and `h1`/`h2` are short unfoldings or thin wrappers over existing API. The `conjOn_cube` calc and the `hττ` and `hτε` calcs are one-line `group` calcs. I report only the repeated center-transport argument. This is a small shared lemma over existing Mathlib API, so the benefit is moderate. I did not compile the proposed rewrites.

findings.problem: Both proofs transport the center cardinality along a `MulEquiv` with the same three-step argument. First rewrite `Nat.card (center K)` as the card of `(center K).map e`, then rewrite that as `center X` using `map_center_eq`, then continue with the numeric bound. The block is spelled out twice (lines 205–208 and 231–234), and `hbot` (lines 221–225) re-derives the same `map_center_eq` fact for the `⊥` case. Mathlib already has `Subgroup.centerCongr`, an isomorphism of the centers, so the manual `map`/`card_map_of_injective` detour is unnecessary.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one private lemma before `rank2Good_of_mulEquiv`:
`theorem card_center_eq_of_mulEquiv {A B : Type*} [Group A] [Group B] (e : A ≃* B) : Nat.card (center A) = Nat.card (center B) := Nat.card_congr (Subgroup.centerCongr e).toEquiv`.
Proof sketch: `centerCongr` is a `MulEquiv` between the two centers, and `Nat.card` is invariant under an `Equiv`.

Use in `rank2Good_of_mulEquiv`: the second goal becomes `(card_center_eq_of_mulEquiv e).trans_le hZ`, which replaces the 5-line calc.

Use in `of_center_ne_bot`: the `SL(3,F4)` branch becomes `(card_center_eq_of_mulEquiv e).trans sl3F4_card_center`. `K` is a `Subgroup G` with `G : Type`, so universe levels are unproblematic.

For `hbot`, `Nat.card (center X) = 1` can be used instead of the `map_eq_bot` argument. This needs `Finite`, which holds for `K ≤ G` with `[Finite G]`, together with `Subgroup.card_eq_one`. If that is awkward, leave `hbot` as is. No new imports are required.
findings.benefit: The shared fact "isomorphic groups have equinumerous centers" is stated once, using the existing Mathlib equivalence `Subgroup.centerCongr`. Both call sites shrink from a 4–5 line calc to one term. A future third shape (as the `PSL`/`SL`/`A₁₁` case split suggests) only needs `card_center_eq_of_mulEquiv e`, and the `map`-based plumbing is no longer repeated.
